en.title: 7 Must-Watch Netflix Gems This Week: From Thrills to Heartwarming Tales
en.summary: Discover your next binge-worthy obsession with our curated picks of the week's best on Netflix, blending critically acclaimed dramas with pure entertainment.
en.body:
This week's Netflix lineup is a treasure trove for discerning viewers, offering a diverse range of stories that are too good to miss. From gripping thrillers to heartwarming romances and eye-opening documentaries, there’s something to satisfy every mood.

## 1. Animals
This political thriller, directed by and starring Ben Affleck, plunges you into a world of high-stakes intrigue and moral ambiguity. Affleck’s masterful direction and compelling performance drive a narrative that questions the lengths people will go to for power, making it a must-watch for fans of complex storytelling.

## 2. Sacrifice
Get ready for an exhilarating ride with this action-satire featuring the dynamic duo of Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy. It masterfully blends adrenaline-pumping sequences with sharp wit, delivering a unique cinematic experience that pokes fun at genre conventions while keeping you on the edge of your seat.

## 3. Midnight Girls
Immerse yourself in the poignant beauty of this Filipino drama that explores the complexities of friendship and growing up. The film offers a sensitive portrayal of its characters' journeys, resonating with universal themes of love, loss, and self-discovery.

## 4. Therapy Done Right
Argentine cinema shines with this darkly comedic gem that pushes the boundaries of conventional therapy. A psychoanalyst's unconventional methods to help a blocked novelist create a hilarious and thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, proving that sometimes, the cure is stranger than the disease.

## 5. Love Actually
No holiday season is complete without this iconic British rom-com. With its interwoven tales of love, loss, and laughter set against the backdrop of festive London, the film’s star-studded cast, including Hugh Grant and Emma Thompson, delivers a heartwarming experience that has cemented its place as a perennial favorite since its 2003 release.

## 6. Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
Kenneth Branagh's ambitious 1994 adaptation of the gothic classic is a visually stunning and thematically rich exploration of ambition and its consequences. Starring Branagh himself alongside Robert De Niro as the Creature, this version delves deep into the philosophical questions at the heart of Mary Shelley's enduring novel.

## 7. SCTV: The Greatest Show You've Never Heard Of
This documentary shines a spotlight on the legendary, yet often overlooked, sketch comedy series that rivaled SNL in its heyday. It’s a fascinating deep dive into the creative genius and chaotic energy behind a show that influenced a generation of comedians, offering a nostalgic trip for comedy aficionados.

Bottom Line: This week's Netflix picks offer a rich tapestry of genres and global perspectives, ensuring a captivating viewing experience for every taste.

content_raw: This past weekend on the big screen, few would be surprised to learn that director Kitao Sakurai 's live-action Street Fighter movie topped the box office charts, despite facing backlash from critics worldwide . With more than $50 million in its opening weekend, Street Fighter KO'd the box office competition, but still didn't come out of the weekend as the most talked-about title. That went to the new documentary You Can See Everything , which scored a huge $15 million haul from just 855 theaters, as well as some of the most impressive reviews of the decade. But beyond the box office, what other movies should you watch this week? With that in mind, here's a list of three movies you should stream on Netflix .
